title: Platform pulse — control plane & auth standup (2026-05-06)
content:
Meeting: Platform engineering weekly pulse (control plane, routing, auth, quotas)
Date: 2026-05-06 09:30–10:00 PT (recurring weekly)
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Liam, Maya, Diego, Zoe, plus optional: SRE on call (Tom)
Status: quick sync; capturing decisions and action items for the week

Agenda:
- Quick health checks: control plane, routing layer, auth service, quotas calculator
- Recent incidents and mitigations
- Rollouts / canaries scheduled this week
- Blockers and help needed
- Action items and owners

1) Control plane health
- Current: config-store migration (etcd -> managed-config) is in canary on us-west-2: 2/6 control-plane nodes (canary set) are on the new controller.
- Observed: config reconciliation latency up ~12% in the canary group (p95 145ms -> 163ms) after bumping serializer. No customer-facing impact yet.
- Cause hypothesis: additional validation step in the migration controller adds CPU spikes when handling concurrent writes.
- Mitigation: throttle background reconciliation and add micro-batching for apply operations. Liam will implement a 50ms debounce for high-frequency keys (task ENG-2410).
- Decision: hold expansion to more nodes until CPU profile shows <10% overhead in canary. Next checkpoint: 2026-05-08 morning.

2) Routing & fallback policies
- Traffic routing: route-by-cost policy tested in staging; fallback to regional-compat model works but we saw sporadic 502s when fallback bound creation raced with model pull.
- Root cause: race in route-instantiation path when model cache is cold.
- Short-term: enable soft-fail path that returns a lightweight cached response (if available) and kick off async model pull. Maya to add a circuit-breaker metric (route.failures.cold-start) and alert at 5/min.
- Long-term: pre-warm model variants for high-QPS routes per annotations. Planning doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/Route+Prewarm+Design (linked in artifacts).

3) Auth service (token management + private deployments)
- Incident last week (2026-05-04): private-deploy customer experienced tokens rotating unexpectedly after vault rekey operation. Impact: short-lived auth failures for specific tenants.
- Root cause: mismatch between vault rotation webhook and control-plane token reconciler; reconciler retried aggressively and created duplicate tokens, TTL mismatch.
- Fix deployed: dedupe idempotency key on reconciler for token-create flow; backfilled reconciler to de-dupe existing duplicates (PR #678). Diego and Zoe drove the hotfix.
- Outstanding: add E2E test that simulates KMS rekey, ensure reconciler honors in-flight webhook. Diego to own ticket ENG-2432.
- Note (ops): recommend customers schedule vault maintenance during low-traffic windows; add guidance to Private deploy runbook.

4) Quotas & billing meter consistency
- Problem surfaced: embedding job with large batch sizes (>=4096 tokens) saw quota delta in billing vs expected usage (~7% undercount).
- Investigation: quota calc uses tokenization heuristics that diverge for some tokenizer versions; embeddings path uses heuristic A, billing meter uses heuristic B.
- Short-term: unify to billing heuristic in the embeddings path; Maya to push change to staging by 2026-05-09.
- Monitoring: add a quota_reconcile job (daily) that compares meter vs usage and raises a ticket if variance >3%. ENG-2440 created.

5) Recent incidents (brief)
- 2026-05-04: Auth rotation (see above) — mitigated, postmortem draft started (Confluence link in artifacts).
- 2026-05-02: Small routing blip (502 bursts) — mitigated by routing cache TTL bump; follow-up: implement prewarm (above).

6) Rollouts / scheduled work
- Control-plane config-store canary: wait until CPU drop to proceed (check 2026-05-08).
- Routing: soft-fail circuit-breaker instrumentation by 2026-05-07 (Maya).
- Auth: E2E test for KMS rekey scenarios (Diego) by 2026-05-13.
- Quotas: billing heuristic unification for embeddings (Maya) staging by 2026-05-09, prod after 48h of no regressions.

7) Blockers / help needed
- We need SRE assistance to reproduce the control-plane CPU spike under load with same validation payloads. Action: Aisha to file ENG-2450 with a reproducible load script and request SRE pairing.
- Security review pending for token reconciler dedupe change — security sign-off required before full rollout to prod. Zoe to loop in security team and request formal review (SEC-PR-120).

8) Action items (owner — due)
- Liam: implement 50ms debounce for config apply in canary controller — due 2026-05-07 (ENG-2410).
- Maya: add route.failures.cold-start metric and soft-fail circuit-breaker — due 2026-05-07.
- Diego: implement E2E test for KMS rekey -> reconciler behavior — due 2026-05-13 (ENG-2432).
- Maya: unify embeddings path to billing token heuristic in staging — due 2026-05-09 (ENG-2440).
- Zoe: request security review for token dedupe change and attach checklist — due 2026-05-08.
- Aisha: open ENG-2450 with reproducible load profile and request SRE pairing — due 2026-05-06 (today).

Notes to self / Todo (Aisha):
- Remind product about planned guidance update for Private deploy runbook (vault maintenance) — add short note to next product sync.
- Verify that we have a paged rollback plan for the config-store canary (if we see >10% CPU overhead) — checklist in Confluence.

Appendix / quick artifacts referenced:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/678 (token reconciler dedupe)
- Jira: ENG-2410, ENG-2432, ENG-2440, ENG-2450
- Confluence: Config Store Migration, Route Prewarm Design, Auth Postmortem (draft)
- Slack: #plat-controlplane (thread: CP-migration-2026-05-05)

If you have updates before next sync, drop notes in the thread or edit this doc. This is a living working doc — leave short status updates under your name.

-- Aisha (notes)
